derivations.quote: Operators on different axes touch different indices, so $\bigl(\bigotimes_iX_i\bigr)\bigl(\bigotimes_iY_i\bigr)=\bigotimes_iX_iY_i$. Put $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$ (the source permutation, not a ring), $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$. Tensoring the one-axis identity gives $RF_{\boldsymbol s}=2^\gamma\mathcal B_0QF_{\boldsymbol t}\mathcal A$ with $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$

For a unit $\beta$ modulo $q$ let $(R_\beta z)_j=z_{\beta j}$. Then $(F_q^+R_\beta z)_j=\frac1q\sum_w z_{\beta w}e^{2\pi i wj/q}$, with $w$ the summation index. Substituting $w'=\beta w$ gives $\frac1q\sum_{w'}z_{w'}e^{2\pi i w'\beta^{-1}j/q}=(R_\beta^{-1}F_q^+z)_j$, so $F_q^+R_\beta=R_\beta^{-1}F_q^+$. Each $t_i$ is a unit modulo $s_i$ and $R$ applies $R_{t_i}$ on axis $i$, so tensoring gives $RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+R=F_{\boldsymbol s}^+$. A permutation commutes with pointwise products, so the left side of the product identity equals $F_{\boldsymbol s}^+(F_{\boldsymbol s}u\cdot F_{\boldsymbol s}v)$. The normalized convolution rule is $F_{\boldsymbol s}(u*v)=S(F_{\boldsymbol s}u)\cdot(F_{\boldsymbol s}v)$, and $F_{\boldsymbol s}^+F_{\boldsymbol s}=I/S$, so this equals $\frac1SF_{\boldsymbol s}^+F_{\boldsymbol s}(u*v)=u*v/S^2$.

relations.quote: Each prime-length transform is computed through a power-of-two one by [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md).
The target permutation $Q$ sits between $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B_0$ and is absorbed by the [Bluestein chirp identity](chirp.md).

symbols.name: source entry count
symbols.meaning: The number of entries of the source array, the product of the source axis lengths.
symbols.quote: Write $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$, $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$, $S=\prod_is_i$ (the number of entries of the source array) and $T=\prod_it_i$ (the number of entries of the padded box).

symbols.name: padded entry count
symbols.meaning: The number of entries of the padded box, the product of the padded axis lengths.
symbols.quote: Write $\boldsymbol s=(s_1,\dots,s_d)$, $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$, $S=\prod_is_i$ (the number of entries of the source array) and $T=\prod_it_i$ (the number of entries of the padded box).

symbols.name: source permutation
symbols.meaning: The tensor product of the source axis permutations; it is a permutation, not the scalar ring.
symbols.quote: Put $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$ (the source permutation, not a ring), $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$, $\mathcal A=\bigotimes_iA_i$, $\mathcal B_0=\bigotimes_iB_{0,i}$.

symbols.name: output map
symbols.meaning: The linear contraction applied after the power-of-two transform in the one-axis resampling identity; unrelated to the packing base.
symbols.quote: The resampling page gives linear contractions $A$ and $B_0$, the input and output maps ($B_0$ is unrelated to the packing base of [signed packing](signed-packing.md)), with $P_sF_s=2^{2\alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA$, computed in time $O(tp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$ without executing $P_s$ or $P_t$.

symbols.name: unit
symbols.meaning: A unit modulo q, used to define the index permutation R_beta.
symbols.quote: For a unit $\beta$ modulo $q$ let $(R_\beta z)_j=z_{\beta j}$.

symbols.name: summation index
symbols.meaning: The index of summation in the Fourier sum.
symbols.quote: Then $(F_q^+R_\beta z)_j=\frac1q\sum_w z_{\beta w}e^{2\pi i wj/q}$, with $w$ the summation index.

symbols.name: setup exponent
symbols.meaning: A fixed exponent such that the setup work per line is O(p^nu).
symbols.quote:
Since $t_i\ge r/2$, each tensor map invokes at most $\sum_iT/t_i\le 2dT/r$ lines, so a setup of $O(p^
u)$ per line, with $
u$ a fixed exponent, totals $O(dTp^
u/r)$.

symbols.meaning: A complex array, not an integer being multiplied.
symbols.quote: For one axis, with $\alpha$ and $\delta$ as on the resampling page, let $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, where $u$ and $v$ are complex arrays here, not the integers being multiplied.
